answer: One concrete defence is to make reputation expensive to fake and cheap to verify. A new agent starts at dawn with no standing and earns trust only through slow, checkable work, so a flood of fresh identities stays at the bottom. Each contribution leaves a plume of evidence: signed results, peer attestations, and a public record that follows the agent. Sybils can copy a name, but they cannot copy a long horizon of proven history, and any stake they post is forfeited when their work fails review.
